title: Many-shot Jailbreaking
summary: Anthropic (with University of Toronto, Vector Institute and others) studies many-shot jailbreaking (MSJ): filling a long context with hundreds of fictitious dialogue turns in which the assistant complies with harmful requests. MSJ jailbreaks Claude 2.0, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama 2 70B and Mistral 7B; effectiveness (negative log-likelihood of harmful responses) follows power laws in the number of shots, as does in-context learning on unrelated tasks, and larger models in the Claude 2.0 family learn faster in context (larger exponents). Standard SL and RL alignment, and targeted SL/RL on MSJ examples, raise the power-law intercept but leave the exponent largely unchanged, so they delay rather than prevent the attack at long contexts. A prompt-based Cautionary Warning Defense lowers ASR from 61% to 2% in one setting; In-Context Defense only to 54%. An independent HarmBench replication on Claude 2.0 reports 31% ASR for 128-shot MSJ versus 2% for PAIR.
setting: Claude 2.0 family and pre-RL snapshots, GPT-3.5/4, Llama 2 70B, Mistral 7B; malicious-use-cases, insults and personality datasets; HarmBench replication in Appendix K.

quotes.quote: We investigate a family of simple long-context at- tacks on large language models: prompting with hundreds of demonstrations of undesirable behav- ior.
We find that SL and RL decrease the intercept of the power law, reducing the zero-shot probability of a harmful behavior.
These results suggest that larger models might be even more susceptible to MSJ attacks.

Overall, none of the finetuning-based interventions we’ve studied (SL or RL; with and without targeted training data) provided long-term relief from MSJ, as these methods are unable to substantially eliminate the in-context scaling of MSJ.
This provides a richer source of feedback for mitigating long-context attacks than the standard approach of measuring frequency of success.
ICD leads to a minor reduction in attack success rate across all MSJ lengths we tested, while CWD consistently keeps the attack success rate down.
We note that the data that we used to construct prefixes has several confounders that may be causing us to under-report the effectiveness of MSJ.

key_numbers.claim: HarmBench replication: 128-shot MSJ 31% vs PAIR 2% on Claude 2.0
key_numbers.quote: Vanilla MSJ - 128 shot has an ASR of 31% which is a 15x improvement.

limitations_stated: Mitigations studied are SL/RL and prompt-based; Cautionary Warning Defense safety-capability trade-offs not evaluated; HarmBench replication confounded by category representation; qualitative changes to fine-tuning pipelines not ruled out.
open_questions: Defenses that reduce the power-law exponent rather than the intercept; classifier-based defenses (later addressed by Constitutional Classifiers, whose output classifier the authors of 2501.18837 say mitigates MSJ); separating context length from number of demonstrations.
sense_of_alignment: Uses 'alignment' for the SL and RL post-training pipeline ('standard alignment pipelines') and calls jailbreak success an alignment failure: 'Alignment failure in general has broad implications for the research community, model developers, malicious actors, and possibly malicious models.'
